document.title: Politburo Session, November 13, 1986
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan Déjà vu? Lessons from the Soviet Experience
document.note: The first detailed Politburo discussion of the process and difficulties of withdrawing Soviet troops from Afghanistan, including the testimony of Marshal Sergei Akhromeev.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CPSU; chaired the Politburo session

mentions.quote: Our strategic goal is to complete this war and pull our forces out in one or, at most, two years.
[Let us] invite Najib here in December.

persons.name: Najibullah
persons.role: Leader of the Afghan (PDPA) government; Soviet-backed successor to Karmal

mentions.quote: Najib has the right thing in mind: he thinks that there needs to be a consolidation of the political leadership
Najib's Politburo did not support him with the idea of national reconciliation

persons.name: Babrak Karmal
persons.role: Former Afghan leader whom the USSR supported militarily; now in opposition to Najib

mentions.quote: when we "agreed to provide military support" to Karmal
Karmal had a simple policy: to just sit there and govern, and to leave the fighting to us.

persons.name: Andrei Gromyko
persons.role: Soviet senior statesman at the Politburo discussion; suggested outreach to the king, the US, London and Pakistan

mentions.quote: Gromyko admits that neither the social conditions nor any of the other circumstances were analyzed sufficiently

persons.name: Zahir Shah
persons.role: Exiled former king of Afghanistan, living in Italy

mentions.quote: turn to the king (who has emigrated to Italy)

persons.name: Viktor Chebrikov
persons.role: KGB chairman; member of Politburo; named to Afghanistan group

mentions.quote: We have not been able to seal the border around Afghanistan

persons.name: Eduard Shevardnadze
persons.role: Soviet Foreign Minister; to head new Politburo Afghanistan group

mentions.quote: We must end this war, and to do that we need to have negotiations on all directions.

persons.name: Anatoly Dobrynin
persons.role: Soviet Central Committee official who called for an 'Afghan Reykjavik'

mentions.quote: We need an Afghan version of the Reykjavik summit.

persons.name: Sergei Akhromeyev
persons.role: Chief of the Soviet General Staff who reported on the military situation

mentions.quote: We have lost this battle. The majority of the Afghan people support the counter-revolution now.
Addresses to Kryuchkov (Deputy Chairman of the KGB)

persons.name: Vladimir Tabeyev
persons.role: Soviet ambassador to Afghanistan, replaced; named to Afghanistan group

mentions.quote: Tabeyev (the Soviet ambassador to Afghanistan) was replaced

persons.name: Murakhovsky
persons.role: Official in charge of supplies to Afghanistan; criticized by Gorbachev

mentions.quote: The first person who should be fired for the failures ... is Murakhovsky (in charge of supplies to Afghanistan

persons.role: Member of the proposed Politburo Afghanistan group

events.description: Politburo session decided to pursue withdrawal within two years, 50% each year, invite Najib in December, and form an Afghanistan group headed by Shevardnadze.
Planned invitation of Najib to Moscow.
Line agreed in October 1985 to ensure a friendly Afghanistan and leave.
CPSU Politburo session on further measures in Afghanistan; Gorbachev sets goal of withdrawal within one to two years.
Politburo line agreed to speed measures to ensure friendly Afghanistan and leave.
events.quote: In accordance with the line that was agreed upon in October 1985

events.description: Politburo group on Afghanistan created with Shevardnadze as head.
Proposed invitation of Najib to Moscow in December.
Tabeyev replaced as Soviet ambassador to Afghanistan to signal Afghan independence.
Gorbachev sets withdrawal timetable: 50% of troops out each year over two years.

key_claims: Gorbachev set the goal of withdrawing Soviet forces within one to two years, 50% each year, leaving a friendly neutral Afghanistan.
Akhromeyev stated the Soviets had lost the battle and that 80% of the country was held by the counter-revolution.
Chebrikov said the border could not be sealed and that the Dushmen had changed tactics.
Shevardnadze argued Najib needed full freedom of action and that authority be concentrated in one center.
Gromyko suggested outreach to the exiled king, the US, London and Pakistan.
The Politburo agreed to invite Najib to Moscow in December and create an Afghanistan group under Shevardnadze.
Gorbachev criticized Murakhovsky for failures in supplying Afghanistan.
